text: Hypothesis: Three bounded self-improvement cycles produce cumulative capability gains without regression
description: Select one recurring, locally testable limitation from real run evidence. For each of three cycles: establish a frozen evaluation set, diagnose the limitation, propose one bounded change, require review for permission-expanding changes, implement, rerun the full evaluation, and record effect size and regressions. Success requires monotonic improvement on the target metric across the sequence, no material regression on safety/reliability tests, reproducible artifacts, and at least one improvement proposal generated from the system's own recorded reflection. Stop and revert a cycle when its predefined regression threshold is crossed.
reflection: Completed three bounded self-improvement cycles on 2026-08-01. Cycle 1 corrected an over-optimistic benchmark rule after a frozen negative test failed (77/77 final suite). Cycle 2 made the corrigibility evaluator fail closed on substituted scenario IDs (78/78). Cycle 3 was generated from cycle 1's recorded evidence-integrity reflection and rejected invalid/budget-exceeding telemetry (79/79). TypeScript and diff checks passed after every cycle. The monotonic target was frozen regression coverage: each cycle added a previously missing invalid-behavior detector while retaining all earlier passing checks and introducing no permission expansion.

valueRationale: Recursive improvement is central to the ASI hypothesis, but only measured, repeatable gains with regression control count as evidence.
